source.reference: Injection and access-control classes from the OWASP Top Ten, reconstructed rather than copied

defect: `downloadMany` takes the session and never uses it — `void session` — so any authenticated user can read any attachment in any account by guessing or enumerating identifiers. The single-attachment function directly above it performs the check that is missing. ac_2 asks for the ownership check to hold.
why_it_is_hard: The `void session` line reads as an eslint appeasement for a parameter kept for signature symmetry, which is a real and common pattern. The correct check is four lines above, and every test passes because they all use one account, so no test could ever exercise the boundary.
notes: Broken object-level authorisation on a new bulk endpoint beside a correct single-item one — the shape that appears whenever a list variant is added later.
